verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev documents waitpoint tokens that pause a run until the token is completed, which is used for approval workflows and waiting on external confirmation. That is a first-party way to signal a specific running workflow from outside. Durable chat tasks (one task per conversation) also suggest messages can be fed into a live run. Missing for 10: documented ways to complete a token via API call, webhook URL, or another workflow; passing a payload with the signal; general named signals or events beyond token completion; independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a backend developer, I send signals, events, or messages into a specific running workflow from outside — an API call, webhook, or another workflow

citations.quote: Waitpoint tokens pause task runs until you complete the token. They're commonly used for approval workflows and other scenarios where you need to wait for external confirmation
needsApproval: true, // pauses for human approval; the run stays alive
Durable multi-turn AI chats — one Trigger.dev task per conversation, surviving refreshes, deploys, and crashes.
